News.title: Parisians sleep outside as Europe’s heatwave moves west with Germany facing record 42C temperatures & travel chaos
News.content:
PARISIANS have been sleeping outside to take advantage of cool night air as the heatwave that has baked France shifts across Europe.

People are turning to city parks to get a good night’s sleep rather than sweltering in overheated apartments amid high temperatures.





Dozens were spotted arriving at Parc des Buttes-Chaumont, in the northeast of the capital, with blankets, hammocks and inflatable mattresses.

France endured its hottest day on record on Wednesday, smashing another record set just the previous day.

Some departments in the west of the country saw highs of over 44C as more than half of the country’s 96 departments were placed on red alert.

The historic heatwave has forced tourist attractions to close and drownings have multiplied as people try to cool off in canals and rivers.

Temperatures have now started to ease as the peak of the heatwave moves on from some regions.

But hospitals remain under intense pressure in the face of severe heat-related emergencies.



The AP-HP authority said its emergency departments treated nearly 3,000 patients on Friday – over a third more than normal.

Temperatures this week have been higher than those during a historic 2003 heat wave that was blamed for 15,000 deaths.

But the AP-HP’s director, Nicolas Revel, said he doesn’t expect as many fatalities this time.



As the heatwave shifts across Europe, temperatures in Germany are expected to hit 41C.

German police have deployed water cannons to cool people down.

Cops are patrolling the streets of Berlin with the riot control gear, misting locals and tourists alike.

The country’s transport infrastructure is being severely affected by the heat this weekend, train operator Deutsche Bahn said.

Two sections of a major road outside Berlin have already burst due to soaring temperatures.



Rail companies have advised against all non-essential travel on long-distance and regional trains across the weekend.

In the western city of Dormagen, dozens of residents of a nursing home were evacuated for medical care due to dangerous heat conditions in the building.

The local fire department reported that temperatures inside the home had reached 35C.



A resident at the home died overnight, but it was not yet clear whether the heat was the cause.

In Italy 18 cities remain on red alert today including popular tourist hotspots Venice, Florence, Bologna and Milan.

Tourists are still trying to cool off in the capital, Rome, seeking shade near buildings and dunking their heads under public fountains.

In the UK conditions are expected to ease across the weekend as the red heat warning drops to amber.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Friday was confirmed as the country’s hottest June day on record, with a provisional temperature of 37C.



It was more than 1C hotter than the long-standing record for June heat set in the summer of 1976.

News.title: The inside story of paranoid loner Derrick Bird who shot dead 12 in 771 minute murder spree before killing himself
News.content:
THE PEACEFUL quiet in rural Cumbria is normally only interrupted by birdsong and the odd tractor rumbling past.

But on one day of horror in 2010 there was also the blast of a shotgun – again and again – as deranged cabbie Derrick Bird launched Britain’s worst massacre since Dunblane.





In 771 minutes of terror he careered around the county taking pot shots at those who he thought had wronged him, close friends and total strangers.

After his shooting spree – which came to an end when he took his own life – 12 people were dead and 11 others had been horrifically injured.

Now, in the latest episode of The Sun’s gripping YouTube series, Inside Stories, we tell how one man turned one of the most picturesque corners of Britain into a killing field.

Bird, 52, lived alone in a tiny terraced house in the village of Rowrah, west Cumbria.



He was well known in the area, drank in local pubs and was a member of a number of clubs including a Sub-Aqua group.

But he was a loner who had struggled to form a new relationship since he split with a long-term partner and he had few close friends.

He holidayed in Thailand with a number of other local men and had met a woman there he considered his girlfriend but they split, triggering mickey-taking from his mates.

That came on the back of regular ribbing by other taxi drivers who thought it was just a laugh, but Bird reckoned it was getting out of hand.



He complained that a tyre had been punctured and milk had been poured into the back seat of his silver Citroën Picasso taxi.

Yet the closest investigators ever got to establishing a motive for his killing spree lay not in his relationship with fellow cabbies, but with his brother and his lawyer.

Bird had developed an obsessive fear that he would be jailed for tax dodging due to thousands in undeclared income.

His twin brother David, 52, and family solicitor Kevin Commons, 60, tried to help him with his financial affairs, but he was so paranoid that he thought they were part of the plot to jail him.

In the early hours of June 2, 2010, dad of two Bird drove the three miles from his home to David’s house in the village of Lamplugh armed with a .22 rifle fitted with a silencer and a sawn-off shotgun.



He gained entry, crept to David’s bedroom and blasted him 11 times.

His body was not found until 11am after he failed to turn up for work.

At 5.14am, Bird arrived at the home of solicitor Kevin Commons, 60. He had known and worked with the Bird family for years and was well liked and trusted by them.

But deranged Bird had become convinced he was also out to get him and lay in wait outside his house for nearly five hours, blocking his drive.

As soon as Kevin got into his car Bird leapt out of his own vehicle and opened fire.



Kevin tried to run back to his house but Bird shot him with his rifle.

As the solicitor was lying critically injured on the ground Bird killed him with a second shot to the head from five yards away.

Having taken care of the two men who were – to his paranoid mind – his main enemies, he drove to the taxi rank in Whitehaven to target those he felt were making his life a misery with their constant mickey-taking and practical jokes.



At 10.27 he pulled up at the back of the town centre rank where the car ahead of him belonged to Darren Rewcastle, 43.

Darren’s mother Betty Scoone later said of her son: “He would do a good turn for anyone. And if he couldn’t do you a good turn he wouldn’t do you a bad one.”

But Bird viewed him as his tormentor-in-chief and when he saw him emerging from a nearby sandwich shop he called him over.

As Darren bent to speak through the open passenger window Bird blasted him in the face with the shotgun. A second shot hit him in the abdomen, killing him instantly.

Bird then shot another taxi driver, Donald Reid, with the rifle, hitting him in the back.



Bird got out of his car and followed Donald as he tried to crawl to safety.

Another stunned cabbie yelled at Bird: “What are you doing?” The gunman turned to get back in his own car and drove off, looping around the one way system to do a drive-by of the rank.

He fired off another couple of shots without hitting anyone before shooting two more cabbies, who survived, as a brave cop flagged down a passing motorist to give chase.

Bird sped off into the countryside, driving through towns and villages where he targeted complete strangers.

In Egremont he spotted secretary Susan Hughes, 57, walking home from shops.



He shot her twice with his shotgun from his driver’s seat, got out, turned her over and shot her a third time with his rifle to make sure she was dead.

He pulled up alongside mole catcher Isaac Dixon, 65, who was checking traps and shot the dad of two twice, killing him.

In a tragic twist he killed a couple in the village of Wilton who were not together but whose paths Bird crossed by chance within a minute of each other.



He first shot account worker Jennifer Jackson, 68, hitting her in the chest with the shotgun and twice in the head with the rifle.

He then drove around the corner and spotted Jennifer’s husband James, 67, chatting to a neighbour.

Bird fired his shotgun from the car, killing the ex-ambulance chief.

Estate agent Jamie Clark, 23, had pulled up by the side of the road to make calls when a colleague contacted him to tell him there had been shooting in the area and to get to safety.

Before he could do anything Bird stopped alongside and blasted him in the head.



In Seascale, a coastal village near the Sellafield nuclear site, Jane Robinson, 66, was delivering Bettaware home catalogues when Bird stopped nearby and called her over to his car.

Tests on her body later showed that the barrel of his shotgun had been touching her mouth when he pulled trigger.

With dozens of armed cops now in pursuit, desperately trying to follow his chaotic and random killing route, Bird sped along a country lane where he crashed into a stone wall near the village of Boot.

He abandoned his taxi and headed into nearby woods where he was found dead a short time later.

Tests show he had knelt down, placed the barrel of his rifle against his forehead and pulled the trigger.



The massacre was over but the devastating effects of it rippled through the years affecting countless people.

To mark the five year anniversary, Darren Rewcastle’s mother Betty did an interview with The Sun and revealed how she still expected him to walk through the door each day.

She said: “They say it gets better over time, I only wish it did.



“I remember it like it was yesterday and it hurts like it was yesterday. Nobody should have to bury their child before them.”

And Terry Kennedy, one of the cabbies who was shot but who survived, incredibly revealed that he bore Bird no resentment.

The pair had been friends for more than 30 years when Bird pulled the trigger and blew away his mate’s right arm.

Terry, who returned to taxiing after getting a prosthetic fitted, said: “He was a bit of a loner but as a bloke he was a decent fella. He just cracked up.

“He’s the last person on earth you’d have thought would do anything like that.”



That summed up the complex question at the heart of the Cumbria shootings – why did Bird do it?

There had been warning signs – a month before he told a scuba diving friend that “Whitehaven will be as famous as Dunblane”, the town in Scotland where 16 school children and their teacher were killed by Thomas Hamilton in 1996.

The friend replied: “Infamous you mean,” and Bird responded: “You will see soon enough.”

And 48 hours before the shooting he said about the taxi drivers who had tormented him: “They are going to get it big style.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fears he was about to be jailed over his tax affairs appears to have been the final trigger.



But no-one among his friends, family, police or coroner was ever able to exactly pinpoint why he felt the need to take so many innocent victims with him.

News.title: Will Labour’s ‘open borders’ scheme fix Britain’s illegal migration problem? VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Will Labour’s ‘open borders’ scheme fix Britain’s illegal migration problem? VOTE NOW

A NEW scheme to bring thousands of refugees to the UK via a “capped, safe and legal” route has been slammed as an “open borders” policy.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is set to announce the new community sponsorship scheme next week, alongside greater powers to throw out bogus asylum applications.



But her Tory counterpart, Chris Philp, blasted the plans, arguing “open borders Labour revealing their true colours again”.

News.title: Distraught parents break silence as son-in-law kills himself in jail after arrest for pushing wife off cliff 20yrs ago
News.content:
THE parents of a woman allegedly killed by her husband after she was pushed off a cliff have spoken of their relief following his shock death just days after he was charged with murder.

David Vander Meer, 48, was accused of murder and insurance fraud in connection with the 2006 death of his wife, Bernadette Vander Meer, at Zion National Park, according to the Washington County Attorney’s Office.





Vander Meer, a former church youth pastor, was due to appear at an extradition hearing on Thursday when a Las Vegas judge informed the court that he had died.

A cause of death has not been released but officials cited “self-sustained injuries.”

The charges came after investigators reopened the case following new evidence that challenged the original ruling that it was an accident.

Bernadette, who was 29 and worked at a Las Vegas hotel, died on August 22, 2006, while visiting Utah’s Zion National Park during a trip from the couple’s Las Vegas home.

Prosecutors say Vander Meer pushed his wife from Angels Landing, a steep and narrow trail known for its dramatic cliffs and dangerous drop-offs.

With Vander Meer now dead, the case against him will not proceed to trial.

But in an exclusive interview with The U.S. Sun, Bernadette’s parents, Richard and Laura Gudenkauf, said they were relieved they would not have to revisit their daughter’s death in court after nearly two decades of waiting for answers.

“I am pleased it’s over. I didn’t want to have to go to court, the anxiety that would have caused me,” said Laura.



“His death confirms what we thought happened to Bernadette.”

“She was such a great girl,” added Richard. “It was difficult to have pictures of her around the house. But now, after everything has come out, we have them scattered without the sadness. I didn’t expect that.”

The investigation was reopened in 2022 after a woman came forward with allegations that Vander Meer had groomed her and had a sexual relationship with her when she was a minor in his church youth group.

Investigators said the woman later told them Vander Meer had made a disturbing statement — that they could only be together if his wife was no longer alive.

Prosecutors say Vander Meer killed his wife during an anniversary trip to Zion National Park in August 2006.



He claimed he had stepped away to reposition the couple’s backpacks before taking a photograph when he heard his wife scream.

When he turned around, he said, she was gone.

It was also revealed Vander Meer dramatically increased the couple’s life insurance coverage before the trip, raising each policy from $150,000 to $550,000.

After Bernadette’s death, he collected a $567,439 insurance payout and spent the money on what investigators described as an extravagant lifestyle.

Neither Richard nor Laura said they ever trusted Vander Meer from the beginning of his relationship with their daughter.



“He had an uncomfortable look in his eye,” said Richard. “It was his mannerisms too. It’s hard to put your finger on it, but I told her three weeks after they started dating that I didn’t trust him.



“She was a woman of God and the Bible says you should do what your husband says. That’s what she did. She was the breadwinner.

“She made a ton of money on tips working at the casino. He didn’t really want to work but she still followed him. He was a scoundrel, he knew how to groom young women.”

Laura, who lived with the couple for two years, said she often tried to avoid her son-in-law.

“I just got an uneasy feeling every time I was around him,” she said. “I tried to avoid him most of the time. But she loved him. At the end she was getting fed up, she was going to divorce him.

“I became afraid of him. He was taking advanced weapon training and I didn’t want him picking me off too. Our daughter Vanessa, who is special needs, needs me.”



After Bernadette’s death, a co-worker from the New York-New York Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas contacted police with concerns about the circumstances surrounding the case.

The colleague said she had known Bernadette for six years but had only briefly met her husband once, adding that he rarely attended social gatherings or work events with his wife.

Investigators also looked into Vander Meer’s spending after his wife’s death, including the purchase of a Cadillac SUV worth around $50,000 after the couple sold a condominium.

Within a few years of Bernadette’s passing, Vander Meer was dismissed from his church position amid allegations that he hosted parties for underage church members and provided them with alcohol.

He later married the former church member involved in the allegations. That marriage ended in divorce in 2014.



Despite the nightmare suffered by Laura and Richard over the last 20 years, the Vander Meer family were in their thoughts upon hearing the news about David’s death.

“I will say a prayer for them,” Richard said. “His dad Howard is a great guy and a good friend. They are nice people, they didn’t deserve to be put into this situation by a bad seed.”

Laura said she tried to persuade authorities to reopen the investigation about a year after her daughter’s death but was told the evidence was “circumstantial.”

It sadly took almost two decades to find closure, yet Bernadette’s memory lives on in her beloved parents.

“She was a beautiful woman, a woman of God, sang at church, and affected hundreds of people at different churches,” the mom said. “Everyone loved her. She was wonderful.

“We wanted justice and we wanted him to be stopped. We knew it would come some day. I am just pleased it is over.”

News.title: Hilarious moment pet dog sparks chaos at UK’s biggest airport after escaping and dashing across runway
News.content:
A DOG sparked chaos at the UK’s biggest airport by escaping from its crate and dashing for the runway.

Pandemonium broke out at Heathrow Airport when the cheeky pooch made a break for it among British Airways planes at Terminal 5.





Flights were paused until ground support staff could catch up with the four-legged friend.

Footage of the mayhem, shared with The Sun, showed the adult dog exploring the airside area of Heathrow, with the sound of jumbo jets nearby.

He then jogged off, past airplane steps and cargo services vehicles, towards a huge jumbo jet parked on a stand.

Another clip shows the mischievous pet sprinting past British Airways jets on the airfield.

Three yellow emergency support vehicles followed the animal in hot pursuit, dramatically trying to shepherd it away from the live runways.

They passed more parked BA jets as Heathrow staff paused their workload to watch the highly unusual spectacle.



An airport source told The Sun: “This was very funny on the face of it, but a huge security and safety blunder in reality.

“Word of the daredevil dog spread like wildfire across Terminal 5 among BA staff.

“It resembled a cartoon with the emergency services desperately trying to catch the pooch.

“But there will be an inquest into how this happened, because the airside area at Heathrow is locked down.

“No unannounced animal or person should be able to gain access to the aircraft and airfield.



“This is no place for an untethered dog – there are more than 40 jumbo jets taking off an hour at Heathrow.

“It doesn’t bear thinking about what might happen should an animal access the live runways. It’s extremely dangerous for everyone concerned.”

The Sun understands that the frisky dog escaped the crate it was being held in during a flight into Heathrow on Friday afternoon.

On touchdown, as the cargo area was accessed by loaders, the animal made a dash for freedom – sparking the extraordinary antics.

Heathrow Airport said the dog was eventually recaptured and was unharmed by its ordeal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source confirmed that the dog accessed the airfield but told The Sun: “The dog is fine and there were no flight cancellations as a result.”

BA said the dog didn’t travel to the UK on one of their flights.

News.title: Body found in desperate hunt for boy, 15, after he vanished while swimming at beauty spot
News.content:
LAKE TRAGEDY Body found in desperate hunt for boy, 15, after he vanished while swimming at beauty spot

Credit: Solent

THE BODY of a 15-year-old boy has been pulled from a lake after he vanished while swimming.

Cops trawled the Hampshire lake from Wednesday afternoon in a desperate search after he disappeared at the popular beauty spot.





They found the boy’s body this morning, bringing their frantic search to a tragic end.

A statement from Hampshire Police said: “The boy’s family have been informed and formal identification has taken place.

“His family are being supported by specially-trained officers.”

He was last seen in the water at Testwood Lakes near Southampton amid the heatwave on Wednesday.

Police marine units searched the lake for days, evacuating the nature reserve while they conducted their extensive investigation.

The reserve remains closed today with events cancelled until further notice, and the public have been urged to avoid the area.

Wednesday was a sweltering hot day in Hampshire, with temperatures reaching 36C.

The public has been urged to show caution when going into cold water amid the record-breaking heatwave this week.



A rare red warning for extreme heat was issued by the Met Office as the UK sweltered in exceptionally hot and humid conditions.

The teen’s death means four people have now died in bodies of water in the UK since the beginning of this heatwave.

It comes after the tragic discovery of the body of Brody Leach, 22, in the River Severn at Shrewsbury this morning.

Cops launched a frantic search after he “got into difficulty in the water” early yesterday morning.

The force said he has been identified by his family, and requested their privacy be respected.



On Wednesday, a 50-year-old man sadly died after a medical emergency at sea off a popular beach.

Emergency services scrambled to Aberavon beach in South Wales after a man needed to be pulled from the water.

HM Coastguard performed CPR on the man from Cilfrew, Neath Port Talbot, but he sadly died.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Essex Police has also confirmed the death of a 69-year-old man in Clacton.

Officers said they were called to a medical emergency in Marine Parade East at just after 11am on Friday after reports of a man in difficulty in the sea.

The force said in a statement: “Officers, paramedics, the fire service and coastguard all attended. Sadly, despite colleagues’ best efforts, a 69-year-old man died at the scene.”

News.title: Grandma ‘poisoned daughter and 4 kids with cocktail of meds’ as child suffered ‘sharp force injuries’ after note found
News.content:
GRIM new details have emerged in the deaths of two women and four children at an apartment in New York.

Cops have revealed a handwritten note was found at the scene and have also released the preliminary autopsy results that suggest a cocktail of medications were used as well as an unidentified weapon.





On Tuesday evening, cops arrived to the apartment in Mechanicville where they found the bodies of a grandmother, her daughter, and her four grandchildren.

Amy Steadman, 64, lived at the property while her daughter Sarah Myers, 44, and her four children Harper, 13, Hudson, 11, and twins Gavin and Gracelynn, 10, lived nearby.

Now, dark details have emerged about what took place in the apartment with Mechanicville Police Department Chief Bill Rabbit saying a handwritten note found at the scene points to Steadman as a suspect.

He noted that none of the bodies could be identified until the autopsies took place on Wednesday, after concerned neighbors reported not seeing the family for weeks.

One local who called the cops reported noticing “the smell of death” as flies gathered around the windows and air conditioner, she told ABC affiliate WTEN.

The date they died is not yet known, but family and friends have shed light on the disturbing timeline, with fears they may have been dead for around 13 days.



Preliminary autopsy and toxicology reports point to a cocktail of medications being used as well as an unidentified weapon.

Chief Rabbit said at a press conference that investigators found evidence of intentional poisoning from several prescription and over the counter medications.

One child also suffered “fatal sharp force injuries.”

“Evidence recovered during the investigation, including a handwritten note and other circumstantial evidence, strongly suggests that Amy Steadman was involved in the deaths,” Rabbit said.

“However, final determinations regarding accountability will be made only after all investigative findings, toxicology results and medical examiner reviews have been completed.”



Meanwhile, the father of the four children, who was in a bitter custody battle with his ex-wife Sarah, has revealed he was due to pick up the kids to take them back to Utah with him on June 30, just days after they were found.

“No parent wants to outlive their children. It breaks my heart,” he told The U.S. Sun.

News.title: Infamous cold case murder which led to THREE wrongful convictions could finally be solved after bombshell new tip off
News.content:
COLD JUSTICE Infamous cold case murder which led to THREE wrongful convictions could finally be solved after bombshell new tip off

COPS have been handed the names of two potential new suspects as they launch a fresh probe into the unsolved murder of newsagent Phillip Saunders almost 40 years ago.

The 58-year-old was battered to death with a shovel outside his Cardiff home in 1987, leading to innocent Michael O’Brien and his two pals Ellis Sherwood and Darren Hall spending 11 years behind bars in one of Britain’s worst miscarriages of justice.





Michael, Ellis and Darren – known as The “Cardiff Newsagent Three” – were ultimately exonerated in 1999.

South Wales Police confirmed a new review – launched this month – “will assess whether there is any potential for further forensic investigation“.

The work is being carried out by the force’s Major Crime Review Unit “in the hope advances in forensic science will provide the breakthrough needed to identify who was responsible”, the force added.

But The Sun can reveal they have also been handed the names of two potential new suspects who might prove key.



Dad-of-four Michael, now 58, has been leading a campaign to re-open the case and finally find the real killer.

In recent years he has also been working with a pair of retired police officers who have been reviewing some of the documents from the original trial, which Michael was able to get hold of – and has identified two people who may never have been spoken to.

He had a meeting with police on June 19 – just hours before cops announced the new forensic review – and said he was shocked by the good news.

During that meeting, Michael says he gave them the names of the two people and they allegedly agreed to look into the possibility of their involvement.



Referring to the review, Michael told The Sun, which has previously publicised the campaign: “It’s come as a surprise, but a nice surprise – they’re willing to put the money and the resources in.

“It’s exactly what I wanted… I wasn’t expecting this when I went into the meeting.”

He added: “I think they felt under pressure. Your article kicked them into gear – it’s a bit of a coincidence otherwise.



“They’ve told the victim’s family that a review is being carried out and said they’ll leave no stone unturned until they catch the real killer.

“It’s a breath of fresh air.”

Michael and the two ex-cops are continuing to compile a report into their findings.

“The police are willing to work with us – they’ve agreed to investigate the names,” he explained.

He said his understanding is the forensic review will re-examine old evidence gathered, as well as exploring fresh leads.



“There must be something there, but what exactly they’ll be doing they couldn’t tell me,” Michael continued.

“They said it’s not a quick fix, but they said they would pull out all the stops and review everything.”

He added: “I said to the police, forget what happened to me and the Newsagent Three, let’s focus on the real killer and get them behind bars.



“The primary victims are Phillip Saunders’ family. I’ve never lost sight of that. People talk about the miscarriage of justice – it was bad what happened to us, but it was worse what happened to Phillip and his family.”

A forensic review is not the same as formally re-opening a case – rather it is a fact-finding step to evaluate if modern scientific techniques could yield new evidence.

Michael was just 19 when cops arrested him and pals Ellis and Darren after Mr Saunders’ death.

All three men were jailed for life – despite no forensic evidence pointing to them even being at the scene – before being released and cleared over a decade later.

The original convictions were based on a false confession from Darren.



The Court of Appeal quashed their convictions, and Michael was later given an out-of-court settlement of £300,000 by South Wales Police.

It was the biggest pay out by an English or Welsh police force.

No other arrests have ever been made, despite a previous “extensive” reinvestigation beginning in 2003.



Mr Saunders, 58, who ran multiple news kiosks, including at Cardiff Central bus station, was attacked in his back garden on the night of October 12 1987 – and died five days later in hospital.

On the evening of the fatal attack, Mr Saunders collected the £500 kiosk takings, went for a pint, then headed home.

He was then fatally attacked with a shovel.

Following his release from prison, Michael has rebuilt his life and even had the chance to meet Mr Saunders’ sister Phoebe and nephew David in a café in Cardiff.

And he now even keeps a picture of them by his front door to remind him of what is at stake in the case – justice for the Saunders family.



“I always wanted to meet them and tell them I didn’t do this,” he previously told The Sun. “It was a very important and emotional moment.”

Michael, as well as Darren and Ellis, were convicted largely based on Darren’s confession, in which he claimed he had acted as a lookout for the others during a “robbery that went wrong”.

However, when the Criminal Cases Review Commission ordered an appeal, the unreliability of the confession was emphasised.



Darren was suffering from antisocial personality disorder and had later retracted the statement – and there was never any forensic evidence tying the three friends to the scene.

The trio were then convicted and jailed for life in 1988.

Describing his time inside, Michael said: “I didn’t have it easy.”

However, he eventually pulled himself “out of the mire”, teaching himself to read and write properly, before studying law.

Michael said: “The only person who was going to get me out of prison was me.”

He would write 70 letters a week to MPs and journalists “without fail”.

Michael would go on to change the law seven times, including a landmark 1999 House of Lords judgement which established that a prisoner has a right to oral interviews with journalists to investigate a potential miscarriage of justice.

The Criminal Cases Review Commission would eventually order a review of South Wales Police in relation to Mr Saunders’ death.

Conducted by Thames Valley Police, the 1998 review was a turning point for Michael, Ellis and Darren, uncovering over 100 breaches of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act by the force during the Cardiff Newsagent Three murder investigation.

The report was so “damning”, the trio were all released on bail two days before Christmas that same year.



On December 17 1999 the Court of Appeal officially quashed the three men’s convictions – and in October 2006 Michael was given £300,000 in an out of court settlement.

South Wales Police said: “South Wales Police is carrying out a review of exhibits to assess whether there is any potential for further forensic investigation.

“This work is being carried out by the force’s Major Crime Review Unit in the hope that advances in forensic science will provide the breakthrough needed to identify who was responsible for Phillip Saunders murder in 1987.

“Mr Saunders’ family and others affected by this case have been informed and our thoughts continue to be with them.”

News.title: Kirkby police incident: 'Body found in road' as officers swarm UK street
News.content:
Kirkby police incident: 'Body found in road' as officers swarm UK street

A man has been found dead on a residential street in Kirkby, Liverpool, with Merseyside Police having launched an investigation into the 'unexplained' discovery

View 2 Images Emergency services at the scene this afternoon (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Police have launched a probe after a man in his 30s was found dead on a residential street in Liverpool.

‌



Merseyside Police said he was discovered on Kersey Road in Kirkby at around 12.50pm today. Officers are currently treating the death as "unexplained".

‌



Witnesses described seeing a man "lying on the floor" before a cordon and a number of white tents were erected at the scene.

‌



One man living nearby said his friend's daughter had found the man, who had facial injuries and did not have shoes on, reports the Liverpool Echo.

A Merseyside Police spokesperson said: "We can confirm that an investigation is underway following the death of a man in Kirkby.

‌



View 2 Images A cordon on Kersey Road, Kirkby (Image: Liverpool Echo)

"At around 12.50pm this afternoon, Saturday 27 June, we received a report from North West Ambulance Service that a man in his 30s was found deceased on Kersey Road.

"A police cordon is in place on Kersey Road and his death is being treated as unexplained whilst enquiries remain ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened.

Article continues below

"Anyone with information should contact Merseyside Police social media desk via X or Facebook @MerPolCC. You can also report information via our website, or by calling 101 quoting log 513 of Saturday 27 June.

"Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here."

News.title: Vain Donald Trump releases new limited-edition passport with his own face and a warning
News.content:
Vain Donald Trump releases new limited-edition passport with his own face and a warning

Donald Trump's latest odd moves has seen the eccentric US President share images of what a limited-edition version of the US passport, with his face on it, will look like

View 4 Images Donald Trump have continued to share his bizarre US anniversary celebrations (Image: Pool/ABACA/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump has revealed the inside of a new limited-edition US passport — which includes an image of himself and his signature in another bizarre ego boost.

‌



The US State Department previously revealed it would be issuing a limited version of passports with the President on them to celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence, this year. Mr Trump has finally revealed what the new design will look like, along with a warning to people.

‌



In a Truth Social post on Friday, the US President shared the images and wrote: "The USA’s New Passport, which says, 'Welcome, but be good!' President DJT." It is not clear where in the passport the "but be good" warning is printed.

‌



US launches new airstrikes on Iran and Strait of Hormuz after Donald Trump claims ceasefire was violated READ MORE :

View 4 Images An image of a limited-edition US passport shared by Trump (Image: @realDonaldTrump)

Mr Trump shared two sample pages which showed him looming over his Oval Office desk with a stern look on his face. It also included text from the original Declaration of Independence in the background and his signature below.

A previous sample of the passports included a different image of Donald Trump an had a US flag in the background instead of the Declaration of Independence.

‌



The other page included "The Declaration of Independence" painting by John Trumbull with "United States of America 250" below. This limited-edition passport was announced back in April as part of the country's 250th anniversary celebrations.

View 4 Images Image of a previous design for the passport for America's 250th birthday (Image: AP)

When it was first announced, it was promoted as "a limited-edition U.S. passport to commemorate the historic occasion of America's 250th anniversary", which would feature "custom artwork and enhanced images on the front, back, and inside covers".

‌



This version of the US passport will reportedly be available for "any American citizen" who applies during the rollout and would also be at the Washington Passport Agency, while they are available.

These bizarre passports are just part of Trump weird way of celebrating the 250th anniversary. A UFC fight was held on the White House South Lawn earlier this month.

View 4 Images Trump stands in The Octagon at his "UFC Freedom 250" fight (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

Mr Trump also used the cage fight to celebrate his 80th birthday. The event was billed as a "gift to the American people" but people needed to pay for a subscription to Paramount+ to watch the event.

Around 4,300 guests were on the South Lawn and among them were some famous faces including British boxed Tyson Fury and Facebook boss Mark Zuckerberg.

The 250th celebrations have not ended just yet as the Trump administration, in yet another weird event, will host an Indycar grand prix through the streets of Washington in August. Trump has also claimed the world's largest fireworks display will take place for the Fourth of July.

News.title: Dad received chilling message before learning kids were dead before Father's Day
News.content:
Dad received chilling message before learning kids were dead before Father's Day

Amy Steadman, 64, her daughter, Sarah Myers, 44, and four grandchildren, Harper, 13, Hudson, 11, and Gavin and Gracelynn, both 10, were found dead in their home in Mechanicville on Tuesday

View 5 Images Myers, 44, had been living with her four children (Image: Facebook)

A devastated dad has spoken of the awful moment when his four children were found dead in their home alongside their mother and grandmother in a suspected poisoning.

‌



The six bodies were found inside their apartment on Tuesday in the small town of Mechanicville in New York State. They were identified as Amy Steadman, 64, her daughter, Sarah Myers, 44, and four grandchildren, Harper, 13, Hudson, 11, and Gavin and Gracelynn, both 10.

‌



The horrific discovery was made by police officers who responded to a welfare check, Mechanicville Police Department Chief William Rabbitt said. He said authorities recovered evidence indicating “intentional poisoning” and added that an autopsy had found that one of the children suffered fatal blunt-force injuries.

‌



View 5 Images Brady told how he had learned his children had died just before Father's Day (Image: Facebook)

The chief revealed that a note found at the crime scene, along with circumstantial evidence, “strongly suggested” that Amy Steadman was involved.

Now the children's father, Brady Harmon, has spoken for the first time, revealing how he was involved in a custody battle with Sarah Myers and that the children had been set to spend the summer with him in Utah.

‌



Brady explained how he and Myers married in 2015 but separated four years later, the last time he had seen his children. He spoke to his children for the last time on June 7, he said, after Myers messaged him on June 10 that they were sick.

View 5 Images Brady revealed that he had got a message from Myers on June 10 to say the children were unwell (Image: Facebook)

"She messaged me, 'Hey, the kids are sick, we'll talk to you on the 11th,'" he told the US Sun. On the same day his lawyer sent Myers paperwork about an upcoming custody hearing on the 29th.

‌



“So, I don't know if that pushed them over the edge because like, ‘Oh my gosh, he actually has a lawyer that's going to do his job. And we don't know a way out of this, so let's do the next best thing. He'll never have access to these kids…’ and then do what they did,” he speculated.

Brady said he called police multiple times to ask for welfare checks after learning the children were sick. He told how he would frequently speak to children on FaceTime and tried to get them excited about the coming visit to Utah.

View 5 Images Amy Steadman is suspected to have played a role, police said (Image: Facebook)

‌



He told the New York Post his children were “happy little kids,” adding: “Harper and Grace would show me their drawings, Hudson would show me their cat and Gavin would show me something he built.”

Brady said he discovered his kids were gone just two days before Father's Day. “No mother, no sane mother, parent or anything would sit there and allow that to happen,” he told local ABC affiliate News 10.

“Who could do that to a child, especially your own child or grandchild? It is so sickening to think that they did that.”

‌



Steadman's ex-husband, John Bauman, told Spectrum News that she loved the kids, as did her daughter. He said he did not believe they had anything to do with their deaths.

View 5 Images Harper, 13, Hudson, 11, and Gavin and Gracelynn, both 10, were found dead by police conducting a welfare check (Image: Facebook)

In 2022 Steadman shared a GoFundMe on her Facebook profile to raise money for her daughter to “help get a domestic violence lawyer”. Brady denied the accusations in his interview with the US Sun, saying Myers was the “culprit” rather than a “victim”.

Article continues below

He also shared an allegation that she stabbed him in the face with a medicine dropper during a fight in 2019, adding that his ex-wife was keeping the kids away from him as a way of keeping “control”.

Police have assured residents that there is no further threat to the public, but with few details released about how the tragedy unfolded the small community has been deeply shaken by the deaths.

News.title: Prince George almost as tall as mum Kate Middleton as RAF visit shows off growth spurt
News.content:
Prince George almost as tall as mum Kate Middleton as RAF visit shows off growth spurt

The Princess of Wales and her eldest son met with pilots and engineers in a video for Armed Forces Day but fans were left surprised at how tall Prince George was compared to his 5ft 9in mum

View 5 Images Prince George standing with Kate Middleton in a new video (Image: @princeandprincessofwales/instagram)

Prince George appeared side by side with his mother Princess Kate in a touching video honouring the country's servicemen and women for Armed Forces Day.

‌



The young prince, aged just 12 years old, appears to be nearly as tall as his 5ft 9in mum, in a video shared on Instagram to their millions of followers. Prince George was invited to sit in an aircraft from the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, during a royal visit to RAF Coningsby in Lincolnshire two weeks ago.

‌



Kate and her eldest son met pilots and engineers while they also examined other planes belonging to the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight at the military air base.

‌



5 View 5 Images Prince George standing next to mum Kate (Image: @princeandprincessofwales/instagram) 5 View 5 Images George in the cockpit of an aircraft at RAF Coningsby (Image: @princeandprincessofwales/instagram)

The fleet is usually used for aerial displays, and is comprised of an Avro Lancaster heavy bomber and two fighters – a Supermarine Spitfire and a Hawker Hurricane. The Princess of Wales, who has been a Royal Honorary Air Commodore of RAF Coningsby since August 2023, was also seen engaged in conversation with RAF pilots and engineers during the visit.

View 5 Images Princess Kate in a video she shared for the special day (Image: @princeandprincessofwales/instagram)

‌



A post on the Waleses' social media account read: "Honouring Service and Sacrifice. Learning about the extraordinary history of these aircraft and meeting the pilots and engineers who keep their legacy alive.

"A powerful reminder of the courage, skill and dedication of those who serve, past and present. Thank you to all those who have served and continue to serve."

Armed Forces Day is a special day to thank and celebrate the armed forces – extending to serving personnel, veterans and cadets – and to honour those who make up the military community. Fans shared their excitement over the video and seeing the mother and son. One person wrote: "Excuse me but when did George become all grown up? What a fun engagement."

‌



View 5 Images Prince George sat in a plane from the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight (Image: @princeandprincessofwales/instagram)

Another person said: "Omg, George grew up very fast." A third royal fan wrote: "Gosh hes as tall as his mum - Love love love this family."

This is not the first time the young prince has shown his fascination with aviation as it was reported George was learning to fly at just 11 years old, back in 2024. The heir to the throne reportedly took his first flight at an Airfield near their old Windsor Great Park home.

Article continues below

He had been soaring above White Waltham Airfield near Maidenhead, Berkshire, during his summer holidays. Kensington Palace last week confirmed Prince George would be attending Eton College this September.

The 12-year-old will be following in the footsteps of his dad, who also went to the elite public school where multiple politicians, actors and royals also attended.

News.title: Strait of Hormuz threat level now 'substantial' as Trump renews strikes on Iran
News.content:
The threat level in the Strait of Hormuz has been increased (file)

The threat level in the Strait of Hormuz has been increased following attacks on merchant vessels - it comes after the US launched strikes on Iran last night

The UKMTO raised the threat level in the Strait of Hormuz to "substantial" following attacks on merchant vessels.

It came after the US launched strikes on Iran last night. Donald Trump had been asked about whether the US would respond following a drone attack a day earlier on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. “You’ll find out,” he said.

“I don’t like the fact that they took a shot yesterday, actually four of them,” Trump said at the White House. When asked why there would be strikes when Trump has insisted talks with Tehran are going well, Trump said of Iran: “They’re a little bit different.”

News.title: King Charles issues statement after Venezuela earthquake as death toll nears 1,000
News.content:
Two powerful earthquakes rocked Venezuela this week with at least 920 people confirmed dead so far - King Charles has sent a message of sympathy to the country

A British search and rescue team has been deployed to Venezuela as the death toll from the double earthquake has surged to nearly 1,000.

The team of 68 - made up of personnel from fire brigades across the country - left RAF Brize Norton on Friday along with six specialist search dogs and humanitarian staff.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer said: "My thoughts are with the people of Venezuela following this week's devastating earthquakes." Meanwhile King Charles said he and the Queen "send our profound sympathy" to those impacted.

At least 920 people have died and thousands more left injured after Venezuela was rocked by two devastating earthquakes on Wednesday night - with the figure expected to rise significantly as around 50,000 remain missing. More than 8,000 people have been found alive.

News.title: Man who encouraged rape of baby and eight-year-old jailed after undercover operation
News.content:
Man who encouraged rape of baby and eight-year-old jailed after undercover operation

Mark Craig, 56, has been jailed after sending messages about sexually abusing children to a man he believed had access to young girls - he was actually speaking to a police officer

View Image Mark Craig, 56, has been jailed (Image: NEROCU)

A man who encouraged the rape of a baby and an eight-year-old child has been jailed.

‌



Mark Craig sent descriptive messages about sexually abusing children to a man he believed had access to young girls, including a baby.

‌



Craig, 56, sent explicit images and videos of himself and persisted to send messages to the man in February this year. But he didn’t realise he was actually speaking to a police officer who was carrying out an investigation.

‌



He has now been jailed at Newcastle Crown Court following a complex police operation by officers from the North East Regional Organised Crime Unit (NEROCU), Chronicle Live reports.

Married couple jailed as WhatsApp messages expose sick images of young child READ MORE :

Officers arrested Craig in March and he was subsequently charged with arrange/facilitate the commission of a child sex offence, making an indecent image of a child and distributing an indecent image of a child. Craig appeared at Newcastle Crown Court and pleaded guilty to all charges.

‌



Craig, from the Westerhope area in Newcastle, appeared before the same court on Friday and was sentenced to seven years and six months in prison.

Speaking after the sentencing, NEROCU Detective Inspector Hull said: "Thankfully this investigation has resulted in the sentencing of a dangerous paedophile who was a serious threat to children.

"This was down to the hard work of officers who do an incredibly difficult job trying to identify these predators and bring them to justice.

Article continues below

"Under Operation Sentinel, our regional approach to tacking serious and organised crime, we will continue to investigate these online offences to safeguard children."

If you have concerns about child abuse or want to report a crime, then you can contact your local police force via their website or by calling 101. Always dial 999 in an emergency. Alternatively, you can contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history
News.content:
Each morning that Venezuelans wake to the aftermath of the dual earthquakes, it is a little darker, a little grimmer.

It means another night in which prayers for the miraculous recovery of missing loved ones went unanswered, in which the fitful sleep of the survivors is interrupted by nightmares of collapsed buildings and moments of sheer panic.

For ex-policeman Jan Carlos Roa Garcia and his family, it was another night sleeping rough. Their building in Caracas wasn't brought down but is too dangerous to return to.

Tears rolling down his cheeks, he says he's not sure he even knows how to rebuild his family's life again.

"If I was 30 and not 50, then maybe. But I don't know where to begin. And so far, no-one in authority has contacted us."

As a loyal public servant, Jan Carlos was careful not to over-criticise the government's response, exhausted and angry though he is.

Musician Zaira Castro had no such reservations.

"We're all pretty frustrated because the government is not showing what it should â a serious display of help," she says in a plaza just a block away from two collapsed buildings.

"It's actually us, the Venezuelans, who are helping each other. We live in a society that has grown into helping each other. We don't depend on the government â that doesn't exist for us anymore."

In the same part of town, called Chacao, the Interim President, Delcy Rodriguez, took a tour with the mayor and was on the receiving end of residents' ire.

"You're campaigning in the middle of a tragedy! The government isn't doing anything for the people," yelled one resident.

On a personal level, I know these streets well. I lived in the affected neighbourhood of Los Palos Grandes in Chacao for several years when I was the BBC's Venezuela Correspondent. My old apartment block was just metres from the collapsed Petunia building, where rescue crews are working around the clock to reach trapped residents. A friend recently posted on social media that her mother was among the missing under the building's rubble.

It was a huge relief to see my old building, the Alheli, still intact and its genial caretaker, Pedro, still outside chatting to elderly residents on the porch. One of them had twisted her ankle on the way down the building. All of them agreed they couldn't remember a tragedy this severe in Venezuela in their lives.

At the scene of the worst-hit areas â particularly the coastal town of La Guaira â the desperation is even greater. The scene around more than 100 flattened buildings is apocalyptic. And as hopes fade, anger grows.

"There are still people in there, we need machinery," says affected resident Eileen Lada. "Help us, please," she pleads.

News.title: Hundreds of Heathrow and Gatwick flights delayed due to thunderstorms
News.content:
Flights at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports have been delayed for up to 11 hours as the heatwave turns to thunderstorms.

More than 800 flights have been delayed in and out of the two travel hubs so far on Saturday and dozens cancelled, many due to the stormy weather. The UK's air traffic control service said delays were expected to continue for the rest of the day.

Some passengers have taken to social media to express their frustration, with one saying her daughter was stuck on an Easyjet plane at Gatwick for four hours before it was cancelled.

Gatwick told BBC News that temporary air traffic control restrictions had been put in place, while Easyjet apologised for the disruption.

More than 400 flights arriving at or departing from Heathrow have been delayed so far on Saturday, according to tracker FlightAware, and another 400 in and out of Gatwick.

Delays to affected flights vary, but Heathrow's live arrival board shows a British Airways flight from Santiago, Chile that was due to land at 10:00 BST but is now not expected to arrive until 21:00 this evening.

Europe-wide aviation agency Eurocontrol mapping shows the most severe air traffic control delays in airspace between south-east England and north-western Europe, where the storm clouds are currently located.

However, other UK airports remain largely unaffected.

NATS, the UK's air traffic control service, said "weather disruption was expected to continue through the rest of the day" after "forecasted severe weather across the south east of England".

The thunderstorms developed overnight - bringing rain and lightning to parts of the UK - following a record-breaking heatwave, with the hottest ever June high of 37.3C recorded in Suffolk on Friday.

An amber warning for extreme heat is in place until Sunday morning for parts of eastern and south-east England - while the thunderstorm to the south of the UK is forecast to worsen throughout Saturday afternoon.

Eurocontrol said a "broad area of hot, unstable air" stretching from northern Spain to southern Sweden was likely to see further storm-cloud development overnight, adding that there was "a large degree of uncertainty" over when and where they would develop.

Flights are having to avoid the area with turbulent conditions, having a knock-on effect on schedules.

News.title: Are we in for a summer of serial heatwaves?
News.content:
Over the last two months the UK has experienced two heatwaves, which have shattered significant, long-standing temperature records.

This hasn't happened since 1911.

And we're still relatively early in the summer with our hottest weather normally coming in late July and into August.

While the current June heatwave will gradually come to an end over the weekend with a return to more average conditions next week, there are already indications that we could see more heatwaves this summer.

It has been a bit of a weather rollercoaster since May when a large area of high pressure - known as a 'heat dome' - sat across the UK bringing dry, sunny and very warm weather. A new May record temperature of 35.1C was set in Kew Gardens, London.

June - and the start of meteorological summer - then started on a wet and much cooler note with temperatures dropping to well below average.

Low pressure from the Atlantic brought a series of weather fronts with the whole of June's rainfall in just the first half of the month.

Weather patterns shifted again and in a dramatic turnaround we've just experienced another intense heatwave with the June all-time temperature record broken.

News.title: Mahmood announces new refugee sponsorship route into UK
News.content:
The Home Office has vowed to introduce new "capped safe and legal" routes for refugees to come to the UK from later this year.

The department said it would allow organisations like universities, community groups and businesses to sponsor refugees who applied to come to the UK, a model based on Canada's asylum system.

The government also said it would press ahead with changes to how human rights and modern slavery laws are applied to asylum applications to root out what it described as "vexatious" claims.

The Conservatives said no extra people should be let into the country until illegal immigration was stopped while Reform UK said it would reverse the scheme if elected to government.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the new system would protect "genuine refugees" while "closing loopholes that have been too often abused".

"Britain has always offered sanctuary to those â¯fleeing warâ¯andâ¯persecution," she said.

"But this system only survives if the public trustsâ¯that it is fair,â¯ controlled, and notâ¯open toâ¯abuse."

Mahmood is attempting to shore up support for her immigration bill before Andy Burnham's expected rise to prime minister. It is set to be put before the Commons next week and its more hardline elements could be opposed by some Labour MPs.

Earlier this year, she took inspiration from Denmark with an asylum system shake-up giving only temporary protection to refugees and doubling the time migrants must wait to gain permanent residency.

The reforms have angered some in Labour who feel there should be more safe and legal routes to the UK to help prevent small boat crossings.

The latest measures, announced on Friday night, draw on Canada's community sponsorship scheme, which has successfully resettled almost 400,000 refugees since being introduced in 1979.

In Canada, 70% of sponsored refugees find work within a year - 30% higher than those resettled through government schemes, according to the Home Office.

The UK already has a relatively small number of refugees who are sponsored in communities under the UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS), but the Home Office said the "vast majority" were supported by local councils.

The government has been under pressure to reduce the number of asylum seekers being housed in hotels at the taxpayers' expense, while illegal small boat arrivals have also undermined public confidence in the asylum system.

News.title: Is Andy Burnham Labour's saviour, or just its best bet?
News.content:
"Affable", "warm", and a close ally says he's a "really nice person â politics is a contact sport and it's not contrived".

One MP calls him a "good bloke", adding that "sound would be the Manchester word". They describe his "social dexterity": an ability to communicate with colleagues and the public in real life and on social media.

But there is a niggling question among many of his colleagues and, in fact, expressed neatly on his Facebook page, where a member of the public wrote: "I have no doubt I'd enjoy a beer with you and we could talk about Joy Division and other important cultural things. But when did that become the thing that determined whether someone becomes the prime minister or not?"

There are nerves in Labour circles about what Burnham would actually do with power. One old friend of his told me: "Andy has huge skills but there have been questions about the extent to which [his] thinking on some of the really tricky stuff has been properly developed".

Another wondered: "Can he shake off the perception that he is a bit of a lightweight?"

Not everyone is convinced he is up to it.

One senior party figure told me: "The eyelashes will deliver for a day, maybe a week. But the scrutiny is brutal. Won't last three months, never mind three years."

Ouch.

Multiple sources believe Burnham appointing his old flatmate and fellow cabinet minister from the New Labour days, James Purnell, as chief of staff is a positive sign. Not just because of Purnell's experience, but also because it has inevitably raised hackles on the left (Purnell has recently worked with big business and is perceived as a Blairite).

The choice was cited to me as evidence that Burnham was willing to make decisions that would upset people. This has been reassuring to some in the party. A prime minister's job is to make choices bound to infuriate one group or another and frankly, there is concern that Burnham might find that hard.

One government source told me: "The thing is he loves to be loved and likes to be liked. He has to be ready to be unpopular â and he will have to face the trade-offs â mayors don't face trade-offs".

One of his old colleagues says: "He is quite emotional, he has feelings." They question "how you balance that with the need for tough skin, the need to see things through and to take very exposed positions".

But you don't spend more than two decades in politics worrying only about pleasing people. Burnham gladly irritated the Labour leadership on a regular basis when Keir Starmer was in charge.

And one ally who worked closely with him in government in the late noughties said his talent was not just being nice: "He never takes no for an answer".

They recall battles between the government and "hostile permanent secretaries" towards the end of Labour's time in power, who they say were "hoarding money for the incoming Tory government".

"He went to war with them and won," Burnham's ally recalls. "It was astonishing".

Some of the doubt stems from a perceived lack of clarity over what Burnham wants to do, beyond get into No 10. And we know he really wants to do that.

This will be third time lucky after running for the leadership and failing in 2010 and 2015. We're used to hearing his rhetoric about change, about making the country more equal, about looking after communities that have been left behind like Makerfield, his new constituency. "Vote Andy - For Us'" goes the tagline.

But when it comes to specifics, it can feel like a bit of a blur.

That's why there is a hot political frenzy around who'll be his chancellor. All the talk in Westminster is of whether he'll pick Ed Miliband, on the soft left, or Wes Streeting, from Labour's right, or Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. Whoever he picks in the end (and perhaps it will be someone else altogether like Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden, less eager to see himself in a political story), the argument has become a proxy for Burnham's overall sense of direction.

News.title: Who are the Panama players England need to look out for?
News.content:
Panama's second World Cup is in danger of finishing the same way as their first in 2018, when they lost all three group games - including 6-1 against England.

A sixth-straight World Cup defeat on Saturday would equal the longest 100% losing record in the tournament's history.

Panama's experienced squad - which is both the oldest and most-capped at this World Cup - are only playing for pride following their early elimination.

BBC Sport has picked out five players who could be key if they are to cause a seismic upset against England.

News.title: Iran takes swipe at US' 'unfair treatment' and throws down gauntlet to Fifa
News.content:
Iran coach Amir Ghalenoei says his nation have been treated "unfairly" by the United States during the World Cup and called on Fifa to intervene in the future.

Iran have been competing at the World Cup against the backdrop of the country's conflict with the United States and Israel.

Their World Cup training base was switched from Arizona to Tijuana in Mexico before the tournament began, and they faced travel restrictions throughout.

For their first two matches in Los Angeles, Iran's squad was only allowed to enter the United States the day before the match and had to leave again on the same day as the game, under the terms of their visas.

Iran drew their final Group G match 1-1 with Egypt to leave their hopes of reaching the last 32 in the balance.

Travel restrictions were eased for the game in Seattle, allowing them to arrive two days early, but they had to return to Tijuana after the match.

Ghalenoei said: "To my players and the team, I want to say to them I'm proud of them. What these young people, these players have done, it should be written in history because the host country treated us very unfairly.

"Despite all of these problems, we've been able to perform well and the world is proud of Iranians and our team.

"I urge Fifa: don't let hosts treat players and teams the same way in future World Cups."

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has previously commented that the organisation did well to ensure Iran could compete at the World Cup at all.

"When people were saying it would be impossible for Iran to come to the World Cup, I promised them that they would come," Infantino said before the tournament began.

"I don't know who else would have been able to ensure in these circumstances - which we could not influence - Iran could come and play."

Infantino later visited the Iran dressing room after their opening draw with New Zealand.

News.title: How completing the World Cup sticker book is like having a second job
News.content:
My name is Sophie, I'm a mum, and it's a little after midnight. My partner wants to turn off the light and go to sleep, but I'm still frantically typing on my phone.

Is it work or family problems keeping me up late?

It's neither.

Instead, I'm in the middle of tense negotiations with a man called Jamie who lives in Bromley, almost 180 miles away from my Shropshire home. We are arranging a swap of 50 stickers for my son's 2026 Panini World Cup album.

Filling it has become like a full-time job.

While most people have been finishing work and sitting back to enjoy the group stages of the tournament, I am spending hours verifying our needs and arranging trades. I now fear stepping into the supermarket due to the cost sticker packs are adding to the weekly grocery shop.

News.title: Lightning causes fires and serious house damage
News.content:
Fire crews across Sussex and Kent have been battling half a dozen blazes caused by lightning strikes in the early hours of the morning.

In Crawley, firefighters are dealing with a blaze in Thatcher Close, which West Sussex Fire and Rescue Service said had been caused by a lightning strike.

Houses in Eastbourne and Bexhill were also struck by lightning within minutes of each other shortly after midnight, with four fire engines sent to each incident.

Kent Fire and Rescue Service reported three fires caused by lightning overnight, including in Ulcombe near Maidstone, where six fire engines attended the scene, and two in Faversham.

An East Sussex Fire and Rescue Service spokesperson said the homes in Bexhill and Eastbourne had been "seriously damaged" by the strikes, while further strikes throughout the night had made the operation "more difficult".

The spokesperson added: "Firefighters continued to work at the scene in Bexhill, using an aerial ladder platform as a water tower once the lightning eased.

News.title: UK search team joins Venezuela earthquake rescue effort
News.content:
British specialist search and rescue teams have been sent to Venezuela, where the death toll from two massive earthquakes on Wednesday has neared 1,000.

A Royal Air Force plane carrying 68 personnel and equipment including sniffer dogs and drones took off from Brize Norton airbase on Friday evening to join an international rescue operation.

The British government announced Â£2m of humanitarian funding for Venezuela, where tens of thousands of people have been displaced by twin earthquakes of 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude, which struck seconds apart.

The epicentre of the deadly quakes was around 100 miles (160km) west of the capital Caracas.

Hundreds of aid workers have arrived or are travelling to the South American country to join the search for survivors.

Hospitals in the worst hit areas have been overwhelmed with a shortage of critical supplies.

A website where people can register their loved ones as missing recorded more than 52,000 people as being uncontactable as of 21:00 BST on Friday.

The UK rescue team brings together firefighters and specialists from around the UK, and is coordinated by Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service, with backing from the RAF.

Humanitarian, medical and security specialists have also joined the deployment.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer said: "My thoughts are with the people of Venezuela following this week's devastating earthquakes.

"The UK stands in solidarity with all those affected, particularly those who have lost loved ones, homes and livelihoods."

On Friday, Venezuela's Acting President Delcy RodrÃ­guez said there had been 215 aftershocks recorded since the earthquakes.

A state of emergency has been declared, while airport, rail and transport services have been halted.

Buildings were levelled by the earthquakes and there has been huge demand for aid supplies among those left homeless.

News.title: Tuchel defends full-back selection after James injury
News.content:
England manager Thomas Tuchel has defended his full-back selection policy after confirming Reece James will miss Saturday's World Cup match against Panama.

As revealed by BBC Sport this week, James was assessed by England medics following Tuesday's goalless draw against Ghana after complaining of a hamstring issue.

Tuchel has since confirmed that the Chelsea right-back has not travelled to New Jersey from their Kansas City base for their final Group L game against Panama on Saturday (22:00 BST). He insists James has a chance of playing in England's last-32 match next week.

However, BBC Sport understands that James is a significant doubt for the start of the knockout stages, with England now guaranteed a place even if they were to drop to third in their group.

James started only 20 league games last season because of injury problems, but Tuchel said of the 26-year-old's latest issue: "No-one could see that coming.

"Reece was in good shape and felt very good, so it's a bit unlucky but Ezri Konsa played in the position for us on a high level. We have still no problem."

James' injury - and the calf issue that caused Tino Livramento to return home from the United States - has thrown into question Tuchel's decision to bring just three recognised full-backs to the World Cup.

There was no place in the squad for Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, for example.

Djed Spence, James and Livramento - who similarly had injury problems last season - were the only genuine full-backs selected.

News.title: Body found in search for teenage swimmer in lake
News.content:
Police searching for a 15-year-old boy who went missing after swimming in a lake have found a body.

Testwood Lakes nature reserve, near Totton, Hampshire, was evacuated as police marine units began the search on Wednesday afternoon.

The boy's family have been informed and formal identification has taken place. A file is being prepared for the coroner.

The incident happened on a day temperatures in Hampshire soared to 36C amid a red extreme heat warning.

Police, including marine teams, have been carrying out extensive searches at the 150-acre nature reserve.

In a statement, Testwood Lakes said it was "extremely concerned" to hear of the "serious incident".

The reserve, owned by Southern Water and managed by Hampshire & Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust, remains closed with people urged to avoid the area.

It is the latest in a number of water deaths during this summer's hot weather.

Police recovered the body of 22-year-old Brody Leach after he got into difficulty in the River Severn in the early hours of Friday morning.

A man died at a beach in Essex on Friday, while on Wednesday, a 50-year-old man was pronounced dead at Aberavon beach after getting into difficulty while swimming in the sea off the south coast of Wales.

Several people died during a previous hot spell in May, including a teenage girl in Warwickshire.

Meanwhile, up to 20 teenagers were rescued from choppy seas off the Lancashire coast.

HM Coastguard said the children were helped on Friday evening in Fleetwood after they got into difficulty in rough seas "a significant distance out from the sea wall".

News.title: Welsh teens arrested in Thailand prompting police probe
News.content:
Two Welsh teenagers have been arrested in Thailand prompting a police investigation into the "circumstances" behind their trip.

South Wales Police said it had "limited information" on the arrests of the 17-year-olds from Cardiff.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) has been in contact with Thai authorities, while police officers are "gathering as much information as possible".

"We understand this is a very concerning time for the families and wider community," said the force.

The FCDO confirmed it was "supporting two British nationals detained in Thailand and is in contact with the local authorities".

News.title: Scotland's World Cup hopes at 0.07% - these are results they need
News.content:
First, South Africa beat South Korea 1-0 to snatch one of the top two places in their group, meaning South Korea - who have a better goal difference than Scotland - dropped to third.

After that, Ecuador produced an unexpected 2-1 victory over Germany to finish third in their group with four points and seal a spot in the last 32.

Sweden then held Japan to a 1-1 draw, also qualifying from third place with four points.

Scotland were down to an 6.89% chance of qualification after that, according to Opta, which decreased to 5.26% after Paraguay played out a stalemate with Australia which suited both sides.

Uruguay losing to Spain was some rare good news but Iran's draw with Egypt leaves them with just a 0.07% chance of progressing.

Those results leave Scotland sitting 10th out of the 12 current third-placed sides and on the brink of missing out on a knockout spot.

If teams in the third-place standings finish level on points, the rankings are then decided by goal difference.

There are now only three groups left to be completed, and Scotland need numerous results to go in their favour.

They need Austria to beat Algeria by at least two goals, or for Algeria to win by four goals or more.

They also need Ghana to defeat Croatia by three goals or more and either DR Congo and Uzbekistan to draw, or for the latter to win by a maximum of three goals.

News.title: Boy, 17, dies and three seriously injured in crash
News.content:
A 17-year-old boy has died in a two-car crash near Eastbourne on Friday evening, police say.

Sussex Police said the teenager died after the car in which he was a passenger collided with another car near Shooters Bottom car park, by Beach Head, at about 21:30 BST on 26 June.

A 19-year-old man from Polegate and a 21-year-old man from Hellingly, who were also in the car, and the 21-year-old driver of the second car were all seriously injured.

The force said it was appealing for witnesses.

Det Sgt Ian Foxton, from Sussex Police's serious collision investigation unit, said: "We are aware there were a number of people in the area at the time of the collision and we would ask anyone who hasn't spoken to us or has any video or dashcam footage to get in touch."

News.title: Teens praised for helping collapsed man, 74, get to hospital
News.content:
A 74-year-old man who collapsed in the street after feeling unwell has praised the actions of two teenage rescuers who got him to hospital.

Nick Peacey was waiting for a bus after attending Cardiff's Tafwyl festival when he collapsed outside Cardiff Castle last Sunday night.

Josh and Taylor, both 15, were passing by and went to Peacey's aid as he drifted in and out of consciousness.

They gave him water and called for an ambulance, only to be told it could be a while before paramedics arrived.

Others also helped at the bus stop until the vehicle had to leave so the pair waited with him for an hour and a half before Taylor decided to call his mum to take Peacey to hospital.

News.title: England v Panama LIVE: Team news as Reece James injury sparks World Cup selection headache
News.content:
Reece James has been ruled out of England v Panama and may be out of their last-32 match as well ( Getty )

England’s end to the group stage of the World Cup may not be as straightforward as expected, as they take on Panama tonight.

Although Thomas Tuchel’s side have already qualified for the knockout stage of the tournament, they have been hit by the news of an injury to Reece James, who will miss tonight’s Group L fixture.

In fact, the right back could be out of England’s last-32 game as well, but for Tuchel it is one problem at a time: first, he must decide how to proceed against Panama, who have nothing to lose in New Jersey after their elimination from the World Cup.

Djed Spence, Ezri Konsa, Jarell Quansah, and Trevoh Chalobah are all options to replace James here, while Declan Rice is expected to be fit in midfield after his own injury scare.

Follow live World Cup updates from the Group L game, below:

News.title: World Cup injury tracker: Neymar, Declan Rice and Christian Pulisic updates
News.content:
